CRAS: alert - allow data arguments to alerts Add the ability for an alert to be signaled with an optional data parameter. Alerts triggered in this way can behave differently. Optionally if they are signaled N times with data, they will be called N times. By default similar to normal alerts without data, those with data will combine alerts if they happen rapidly together, possibly only executing the callback once with the most recent data pointer. This will be used to allow data to be passed in to the callbacks so that more callback systems can use the alert infrastructure instead of open-coding it. BUG=None TEST=Unit tests added. Used via cras client monitor in subsequent commit. Change-Id: I96c5a0485dca8b16dbb0f45d3e5114ca1b491abb Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/348653 Commit-Ready: John Muir <muirj@google.com> Tested-by: John Muir <muirj@google.com>

UPSTREAM: fs/timerfd: reject ALARM timerfds without CAP_WAKE_ALARM timerfd gives processes a way to set wake alarms, but unlike timers made using timer_create, timerfds don't check whether the process has CAP_WAKE_ALARM before setting alarm-time timers. CAP_WAKE_ALARM is supposed to gate this behavior and so it makes sense that we should deny permission to create such timerfds if the process doesn't have this capability. (am from 2895a5e5b3ae78d9923a91fce405d4a2f32c4309) BUG=b:29124145 TEST=run a program that performs timerfd_create(2) with a CLOCK_REALTIME_ALARM and ensure timerfd creation fails. Revert "CHROMIUM: iwl7000: pcie: fix RF-Kill vs. firmware load race" This patch reverts commit a2575ed2db3ae2c9c3d535eea3f69823e059d22b. The commit introduce iwl_enable_fw_load_int, which modifies the hardware interrupt register via tran_pcie->inta_mask, from the ISR. This causes a race condition where the ISR thread overwrites the register value from the main thread, when the main thread calls iwl_enable_interrupts. As a result, the alive interrupt is masked in hardware. The driver times out on not receiving the alive interrupt from the NIC, and there is no wifi on resuming from a suspend. BUG=chrome-os-partner:53958 TEST=`suspend_stress_test -c 500` for 20 times on an i3 and i7 samus. Change-Id: Ic83185fed2253f294f3fa4300108e8b2c48b97ee Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/351774 Commit-Ready: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@google.com> Tested-by: Kirtika Ruchandani <kirtika@google.com> Reviewed-by: Sameer Nanda <snanda@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Emmanuel Grumbach <emmanuel.grumbach@intel.com>

net-print/cups: don't let 'nobody' group own anything The security_StatefulPermissions test doesn't like stray users/groups having writable permissions, without having those directories listed explicitly in the test. This highlighted the fact that we're giving 'nobody' permissions, where we really don't want to. We might as well just use the 'cups' group instead, so that if "unprivileged" processes ever end up running as 'nobody', they don't get writeable permission to any CUPS directories.
